subject: Retention clarification: where requests & responses live and deletion triggers
body:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@brightbank.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Where do BrightBank requests live by default / deletion path?

Hi Naomi,

Quick question from the BrightBank security review: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default for a normal hosted API integration (no Dedicated contract)? Specifically:
- Are full request payloads (user prompt + metadata) persisted?
- Are generated outputs (model responses) stored, and for how long?
- What about intermediate artifacts (streamed tokens, KV cache entries)?

Also: what’s the standard process and expected SLA for a BrightBank request to have data deleted (e.g., a legal/DSR request or a customer account termination)? If you have a one-page summary or a short decision tree that we can include in our review, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Maya
BrightBank — InfoSec

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@brightbank.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Where do BrightBank requests live by default / deletion path?

Maya,

Thanks — helpful list of asks. Short answers up front, followed by a concise decision-path and a link to a single-page summary (attached).

- Default capture: For our hosted API (self-serve/standard tiers) we capture request payloads and generated outputs for 45 days by default. This covers the full request/response pair and standard metadata (timestamps, model used, route, truncated headers).
- Prompt vs derived outputs: We classify the original user-supplied content (prompt) and the model-generated output differently for legal and residency purposes — both are captured under the 45-day default, but customers can opt into longer horizons or exemptions via an elevated contract (Dedicated/Private).
- Intermediate artifacts: KV cache entries, transient streaming buffers, and low-level per-token telemetry are ephemeral; KV caches are retained up to 24 hours for efficiency and then tombstoned; streaming buffers are ephemeral and are not written to long-term stores unless a final response is committed.
- Deletion process: Customers request deletion via Support (link below). For standard hosted customers we process and confirm deletions within 7 business days after validating the request, unless the deletion requires cross-region coordination or legal hold. Dedicated/Private customers have contractual SLAs and may require additional steps.

See attached: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf — it’s a one-pager you can include in your review.

If helpful I’ll loop in Karthik for the contractual exceptions and Laura for the enterprise deletion runbook.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — quick addition from a commercial/ops angle: 

- Dedicated/Private customers: You can disable default capture for new deployments, or set retention to an enterprise-controlled TTL (e.g., 0/7/30/90/365 days) as part of the Dedicated contract. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, retention is under customer control.
- Residency: For hosted accounts the default storage region follows account region (US/EU/APAC). For EU residency we provide EU-only storage options on sign-up or via migration for active accounts, and we document the migration-window and artifacts that will be moved.
- Exceptional deletions & legal holds: If you need a deletion to be deferred for investigation or legal hold, we’ll mark the account and surface it as an exception (no automatic purge).

If BrightBank wants a formal amendment to the hosted terms to shorten the default retention or to require EU residency by default, we can scope that as an SOW/contract change (I can share sample language).

-Karthik
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Where do BrightBank requests live by default / deletion path?

Hi everyone — technical clarifications (runbook excerpts below):

1) What we persist by default (hosted API):
- request_payload.json (prompt + request metadata) — stored in encrypted object storage for 45 days.
- model_response.json (final generated text/structured output) — stored alongside request_payload.json for 45 days.
- telemetry logs (tokens_per_request, latency, error_codes) — aggregated and retained for 13 months for product telemetry; these are stripped of full prompt/response text.
- KV cache: TTL 24h; not backed up to long-term storage unless a snapshot is taken (snapshots are explicit and require elevated permissions).

2) Deletion workflow (standard hosted):
- Customer opens Support ticket with account ID + deletion scope (account-level or specific conversation IDs).
- We validate the request and run an automated purge for object-store artifacts (usually completes within 2 business days).
- Indexes and metadata are marked as deleted and tombstoned; final compacting of indexes may take up to 7 business days across distributed shards.
- We provide a deletion confirmation report (artifact list + timestamps).

3) Edge cases:
- If a request has been used in model fine-tuning (explicit opt-in) it will be excluded from automated purge until we coordinate retraining or redaction.
- Backups: backups are on a 30-day rotation; we can scope a shorter backup retention for enterprise contracts.

Attachment: soc2-bridge-annex.pdf contains the relevant control mappings auditors typically ask for.

Let me know if you want a short runbook we can provide that maps actions to Support request templates.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Product Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
